---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 1: generate slides"
---

Step 1 of the paper simulation: the slides (images) of all simulated datasets with their number of
ground-truth objects P. Later steps add the detection counts (TP, FN, FP) for the performance
variants and fit the models.

**Design**

- Four slide distributions (scenarios), each with 40 and 100 slides per dataset:
  - **A, low only:** few objects per slide (median about 4).
  - **B, broad:** wide range of objects per slide, like the MIDOG data (median about 20).
  - **C, bimodal:** like the pathologist data: slides with a moderate number of objects (median about 15)
    plus a group of slides with many objects (about 215).
  - **D, very low:** P = 1 + Poisson(0.5) (P = 1, 2, 3, 4+ with probability 0.607, 0.303, 0.076,
    0.014), as in radiology (one lesion per image is the typical case).
- P = 1 + Poisson(exp(x)), x normal on the log scale (D: x = log(0.5) for all slides); slides with
  more than P_max objects are drawn again (A-C: P_max = 300, D: no upper limit).
- 500 replicates (datasets) per scenario and number of slides; the 40- and 100-slide datasets are
  drawn independently (unpaired).
- Every dataset has its own seed (`seed = seed_base + rep`), so a single dataset can be regenerated
  without the others.

**Seed scheme for all steps** (`01_seed_offsets.csv`)

Every random step gets its own seed, derived from the dataset seed with a fixed offset.

| Step | Seed |
| --- | --- |
| Slides (this file) | `seed` |
| Counts (TP, FN, FP) per performance variant | `seed + 1000000 * variant` |
| Bootstrap | `seed + 2000000` |
| Bayesian post-processing (Bayesian bootstrap, new raters) | `seed + 3000000` |
| Stan sampling | `seed + 4000000` |

**Output** (`simulation/data/`)

- `01_slide_scenarios.csv`: one row per scenario and number of slides with the parameters of
  `simulate_slides()`, the number of replicates, `seed_base` and metadata (R version, RNG kind, date).
- `01_slides.csv.xz`: long format, one row per slide: `scenario`, `n_slide`, `rep`, `seed`, `slide`, `group`, `P`.
- `01_seed_offsets.csv`: the seed offsets of all steps (table above).
- `01_slides_superpop.csv.xz`: the superpopulation of slides per scenario (10^6 slides, same parameters,
  own seed `seed_superpop`): `scenario`, `slide`, `group`, `P`. It is the basis of the population truth;
  the same superpopulation is used for 40 and 100 slides.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# Generate images/slides with a random number of ground truth objects.
# Each slide is in the "high" group with probability w, otherwise "low" (w = 0 gives a single
# group); P = 1 + Poisson(exp(x)) with x ~ Normal(log(median), sd) of the slide's group (the shift
# by 1 excludes P = 0; sd = 0 gives a plain Poisson). Slides with more than P_max objects are drawn
# again (truncated distribution, no spike at P_max).
simulate_slides <- function(n_slide, median_low, sd_low,
                            w = 0, median_high = NA, sd_high = NA, P_max = Inf) {
  df_slides <- tibble(
    slide = seq_len(n_slide),
    # For w > 0 simulate a bimodal distribution of objects per slide
    group = sample(c("high", "low"), n_slide, replace = TRUE, prob = c(w, 1 - w)),
    log_median = log(if_else(group == "high", median_high, median_low)),
    log_sd     = if_else(group == "high", sd_high, sd_low),
    P          = rpois(n_slide, exp(rnorm(n_slide, log_median, log_sd))) + 1L
  )

  # Redraw slides above P_max (same group)
  while (any(df_slides$P > P_max)) {
    df_slides <- df_slides |>
      mutate(P = if_else(P > P_max, rpois(n(), exp(rnorm(n(), log_median, log_sd))) + 1L, P))
  }

  df_slides |>
    select(slide, group, P)
}
```

# Design
```{r}
# Slide distributions (parameters of simulate_slides()); seed_base per scenario and number of
# slides, the seed of a dataset is seed_base + rep
n_rep <- 500
scenarios <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")

df_slide_scenarios <- tribble(
  ~scenario, ~description,                  ~median_low, ~sd_low, ~w,  ~median_high, ~sd_high, ~P_max,
  "A",       "low only",                    3,           0.5,     0,   NA,           NA,       300,
  "B",       "broad (like MIDOG)",          19,          1,       0,   NA,           NA,       300,
  "C",       "bimodal (like pathologists)", 15,          1,       0.2, 215,          0.15,     300,
  "D",       "very low",                    0.5,         0,       0,   NA,           NA,       Inf
) |>
  cross_join(tibble(n_slide = c(40, 100))) |>
  mutate(
    n_rep = n_rep,
    seed_base = 100000 * match(scenario, scenarios) + 10000 * if_else(n_slide == 40, 1, 2),
    # Superpopulation (one per scenario, the same for both numbers of slides)
    n_superpop = 1e6,
    seed_superpop = 900000 + match(scenario, scenarios),
    # Metadata for reproducibility
    r_version = R.version.string,
    rng_kind = paste(RNGkind(), collapse = " / "),
    created = format(Sys.Date())
  ) |>
  relocate(scenario, n_slide)

df_slide_scenarios

# Offsets of the seed per random step (seed of a step = seed + offset; counts: offset * variant)
df_seed_offsets <- tribble(
  ~step,                ~offset,
  "slides",               0,
  "counts",               1000000,
  "bootstrap",            2000000,
  "bayes_postprocessing", 3000000,
  "stan",                 4000000
)
```

# Generate slides
```{r}
# One dataset per scenario, number of slides and replicate, each with its own seed
df_slides <- df_slide_scenarios |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, median_low, sd_low, w, median_high, sd_high, P_max, seed_base) |>
  cross_join(tibble(rep = seq_len(n_rep))) |>
  mutate(seed = seed_base + rep) |>
  mutate(slides = pmap(list(seed, n_slide, median_low, sd_low, w, median_high, sd_high, P_max),
                       \(seed, n_slide, median_low, sd_low, w, median_high, sd_high, P_max) {
                         set.seed(seed)
                         simulate_slides(n_slide, median_low = median_low, sd_low = sd_low,
                                         w = w, median_high = median_high, sd_high = sd_high,
                                         P_max = P_max)
                       })) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, seed, slides) |>
  unnest(slides)
```

# Generate superpopulation
```{r}
# 10^6 slides per scenario with the same parameters and an own seed, basis of the population truth
df_slides_superpop <- df_slide_scenarios |>
  distinct(scenario, median_low, sd_low, w, median_high, sd_high, P_max, n_superpop, seed_superpop) |>
  mutate(slides = pmap(list(seed_superpop, n_superpop, median_low, sd_low, w, median_high, sd_high, P_max),
                       \(seed, n_slide, median_low, sd_low, w, median_high, sd_high, P_max) {
                         set.seed(seed)
                         simulate_slides(n_slide, median_low = median_low, sd_low = sd_low,
                                         w = w, median_high = median_high, sd_high = sd_high,
                                         P_max = P_max)
                       })) |>
  select(scenario, slides) |>
  unnest(slides)
```

# Save
```{r}
dir.create("simulation/data", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write_csv(df_slide_scenarios, "simulation/data/01_slide_scenarios.csv")
write_csv(df_slides, "simulation/data/01_slides.csv.xz")
write_csv(df_seed_offsets, "simulation/data/01_seed_offsets.csv")
# xz compression (from the file extension)
write_csv(df_slides_superpop, "simulation/data/01_slides_superpop.csv.xz")
```

# Check
```{r}
# Number of datasets and slides per scenario and number of slides
df_slides |>
  group_by(scenario, n_slide) |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(rep), slides = n(), seeds = n_distinct(seed),
            share_high = mean(group == "high"), .groups = "drop")

# Distribution of P per scenario and number of slides
df_slides |>
  group_by(scenario, n_slide) |>
  summarise(min = min(P), q05 = quantile(P, 0.05), median = median(P), mean = mean(P),
            q95 = quantile(P, 0.95), max = max(P), share_P_le_3 = mean(P <= 3), .groups = "drop")

df_slides |>
  ggplot(aes(P)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_grid(scenario ~ n_slide, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()

# Superpopulation vs. all datasets of a scenario: the distributions of P should agree
bind_rows(
  df_slides |> mutate(source = paste(n_slide, "slides, all datasets")),
  df_slides_superpop |> mutate(source = "superpopulation")
) |>
  group_by(scenario, source) |>
  summarise(slides = n(), q05 = quantile(P, 0.05), q25 = quantile(P, 0.25), median = median(P),
            q75 = quantile(P, 0.75), q95 = quantile(P, 0.95), max = max(P),
            share_high = mean(group == "high"), .groups = "drop")
```
